punchline: A researcher asked children how long they expected to play an instrument before they had played a note, and the answer predicted who improved.
thirty_sec: Daniel Coyle describes a study in which Gary McPherson followed 157 children learning an instrument. Before they started, he asked each one how long they expected to keep playing. Coyle presents that answer as the factor that most separated the children who progressed from the ones who did not. It couldn't measure skill, because nobody had played yet. Coyle calls it ignition: a child's picture of a future self who plays makes the practice worth doing.
